full: GTA 6 is finally here. It has a ninety-nine on Metacritic. And reviewers who played it for over a hundred hours all hit the same problem.
This game does not explain itself.
So I read the reviews and the hands-on guides for you. And I pulled out thirteen things GTA 6 never tells you.
Quick honesty check. I have not played a hundred and forty hours. These come from people who have, and every source is on screen and in the description.
Number eight is the one that will save your first robbery. And number thirteen might save your whole weekend. Let's go!
Number one. You can't carry everything anymore.
In GTA 5, your weapon wheel held an entire army. That's gone.
Early hands-on reports say you get four active slots. Two long guns, one pistol, and one melee weapon.
Everything else stays in your car, or back at your safehouse. So you choose your loadout before the mission. Not in the middle of it.
The good news? You can swap between your two main guns instantly, without even opening the wheel.
Number two. Your flipped car will not fix itself.
In the old games, you wiggled the stick and your car rolled back over. Not here.
But there's a trick. Walk into the car and keep walking. A prompt appears. Hold Square on PlayStation, and you shove it. Hard.
That flips a car back onto its wheels, for free. And it even pushes a beached boat back into the water.
Why does free matter? Because cars in this game are fragile. Reviewers keep mentioning repair bills. So stop paying for a tow truck.
Number three. Your car door is a weapon.
While you're driving, press Square, and you swing the door open into whoever is standing there.
On a motorbike, it turns into a kick. Perfect for knocking a rival off their bike in a race.
Number four. You don't just smash the window anymore.
To break into a parked car quietly, you use a slim jim. Press Triangle to start. Then sweep the right stick from three o'clock around to nine o'clock, in one clean move.
Do it smoothly, and you're in. No broken glass. No alarm. No witness.
Number five. There's a hidden car menu.
Hold left on the D-pad to bring up the radio. Then push up on the stick.
Now you can roll the windows down, switch on high beams, turn on hazard lights, and drop the roof on a convertible.
You can even tap left or right on the D-pad to use your turn signals. It does absolutely nothing. I love it.
Number six. Click both sticks to find secrets.
Press both sticks in at the same time, and you enter Focus Mode.
If something special is close by, you'll see a ring of sound on screen. That ring points you to a unique encounter you'd normally walk right past.
So if you hear something strange? Both sticks. Every time.
Number seven. The map has a secret color code.
Open your map and look at the buildings. Dark blue means you can go inside. Light blue means you can't.
Rotate the map and you can even find where the doors are. In a world this big, that saves you hours of pulling on locked handles.
Number eight. Case the joint first.
Before you rob a store, walk in like a normal customer. Look around. Find the alarm on the wall.
Then lock on to a security guard, and press right on the D-pad. That marks them.
Now an arrow follows that guard for the whole robbery. You always know where the danger is.
Remember our police video? No witness, no alarm, no stars. This is how you pull that off.
Number nine. Any explosion opens a safe.
No safe code? The game hands you a sticky bomb. But you don't need one.
A grenade works. A rocket works. Even a propane tank works. If it goes boom, the safe opens.
Number ten. You can swim way faster.
On the surface, click the stick once for a speed boost. Click it again for top speed.
That burns stamina. So when it runs out, dive. Underwater, the game uses your lungs instead, and you keep that top speed for longer.
Number eleven. Not every shot is a kill.
Watch your hit marker. Red means that enemy is dead. Yellow means they're only down, still alive, and still on the floor.
That was spotted in Rockstar's own Extended Look. So in a big fight, yellow is not finished.
Number twelve. You can talk your way out.
When a stranger gets in your face, you don't have to throw a punch. On screen options let you calm things down, or wind them up even more.
And Rockstar says the way you keep behaving can change how the world reacts to you. So being a jerk all the time has a price.
Number thirteen. You can retry from a checkpoint.
Reviews say you can now restart a mission from its last checkpoint, whenever you want. Messed up a perfect getaway? Run it back.
Over a sixty hour story, that one button is going to save a lot of controllers.
Now, seven quick answers to the questions everyone is asking.
Is there a performance mode? No. Reviews say it targets thirty frames a second on every console. Even the PS5 Pro.
How long is the story? Fifty to eighty hours. Most reviewers landed near sixty.
Does your hair grow, like in Red Dead? No. You change it at a barber or your safehouse.
Is it on PC? No. PS5 and Xbox Series only, and Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version.
And GTA Online? Critics only played the story. Rockstar hasn't shown them an online mode yet.
How big is the download? Huge. PlayStation asks for over two hundred gigabytes of free space.
And what is there to do besides crime? Fishing, golf, hunting, diving, bird watching, even drone races. Yes. Bird watching. In GTA.
So, quick recap. Four weapon slots. Shove your flipped car. Use your door. Slim jim, don't smash. Click both sticks. Read the map. Case the joint. And yellow is not finished.
Which one are you trying first? Tell me in the comments. And if you found a trick I missed, drop it there too.
